name: Kettlebell Standing Side-to-Side Twist
description:
Stand tall in an athletic stance, holding a single kettlebell by the body or horns with BOTH hands, arms extended straight out in front at about chest height. Keeping the arms straight, twist the bell side to side — rotating through the torso, back through center, and to the other side — while bracing the core to control the rotation and resist being yanked around. The straight-arm lever makes a light bell feel heavy and lights up the obliques, shoulders, and grip. Light bell, smooth and controlled: ribs down, stand tall, and let the core — not the lower back — drive the twist.

Also loosely called a 'gorilla swing,' but that name standardly denotes a different two-kettlebell, wide-stance, bent-over alternating swing — so this descriptive name is used here to avoid the conflict.
